recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中成片的大型母細胞，圓形或帶凹痕的核、細緻染色質與可見核仁，細胞質淡藍色偶有空泡，中間夾雜少數顆粒球，符合 CML 急性轉化中母細胞增生。
features: Sheet of large blasts with round to indented or cleaved nuclei
Fine, dispersed chromatin with small nucleoli in several cells
Moderate pale blue cytoplasm, occasionally with small vacuoles; one blast with deeply basophilic cytoplasm
Few admixed granulated cells including a basophil/granulocyte precursor
Scattered granular debris and red cells in the background
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a sheet of large blasts with round to indented nuclei, fine chromatin, small nucleoli and moderate pale blue cytoplasm, some containing small vacuoles. A few granulated cells, including a basophil-type cell, are admixed, while maturing granulocytes are scarce in this field. Auer rods are not identified. Findings are consistent with blast phase of CML, BCR-ABL1-positive, pending flow cytometric lineage determination.

ddx.vs: Blast morphology is similar, and separation relies on prior chronic-phase history, residual basophilia and BCR-ABL1 transcript type rather than cytology.
Lymphoid blasts usually have scantier cytoplasm and less vesicular chromatin, but flow cytometry (TdT, CD19, CD10 vs MPO, CD13, CD33) is required.
Monoblasts have more abundant gray cytoplasm and are NSE positive with CD14/CD64 expression, unlike typical myeloblasts.
